mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate below 1.0% compresses equity discount rates by reducing risk-free rates, generating positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days as investors shift capital from fixed income to equities.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS < 1.0%, or Rank IC over 5-year rolling windows falls below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: Unemployment rate exceeding 5.0% signals labor market deterioration that triggers risk-off sentiment, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over 5 trading days as recession expectations rise.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) indicates broad consumer demand contraction, triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days as recession risks materialize.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when both HOUST and RSAFS decline, or interaction effect Rank IC falls below 0.04 over 5-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Slowing industrial production (INDPRO < 100.5) during late-cycle expansion signals supply-side constraints that reduce corporate profit visibility, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO < 100.5, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts (HOUST) consistently reflect improving consumer confidence and economic activity, driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days as growth expectations strengthen.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST increases by >0.5% MoM, or Rank IC over 5-year rolling windows falls below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: Core inflation exceeding 3.0% (CPIAUCSL > 3.0) signals persistent inflation that forces the Federal Reserve to accelerate rate hikes, generating negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL > 3.0, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows remains below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent decline in employment growth (PAYEMS) and rising unemployment (UNRATE) indicates accelerating labor market deterioration, triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are positive in more than 50% of periods when PAYEMS declines and UNRATE rises, or interaction effect Rank IC falls below 0.04 over 5-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%) increase discount rates and reduce corporate earnings visibility, causing negative S&P 500 forward returns over 60 trading days as equity valuations contract.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.0, or Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows remains below 0.03.
